name: Supermarket
concept: The small-town self-service grocery of 1989 Everon: the one-storey supermarket that replaced the counter shop in the late 1970s and 80s (a French 'supérette' or a Czech 'samoobsluha'). One rendered hall about 18 by 14 m, a flat roof, plate-glass shop front with a glass entrance and a canopy on the street side, blind side and back walls so shelving can stand against them, and a stockroom, office and WC behind the sales floor. ArchBuilder's SUPERMARKET archetype is that building: one tall storey (5 m), flat metal roof, panoramic front glazing on the front only, a vanilla GroceryStore fascia sign. Its default size (30 to 46 m wide) is a modern out-of-town store, so the spec shrinks it to a village-centre plot and gives it a cream render, which reads as 1980s rather than the profile's metal panels. (Plain white plaster renders near-white in game: the base game's plaster texture is meant to be tinted, and only the coloured stucco materials carry a tint.) Built with Reforger proportions and vanilla doors and windows. The shelves stay out for now: our shop feature fills them in a follow-up (docs/architecture/building-pipeline-spike.md "Supermarket next steps").
